topIssues.title: Error running validation checks on all chains
topIssues.author: vdamle
topIssues.body:
**Bug Description**

Occasionally, the test to run validation checks on all chains - `just validate "*"` fails many checks. Upon looking at the error logs in CI, there appears to be a `concurrent map read and map write` occurring which causes this error. See [CI Job output](https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/github/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/9295/workflows/71929054-0c64-4502-9f89-48506e0e4eac/jobs/38925)

**Steps to Reproduce**

run `just validate "*"`

**Expected behavior**

Validation should pass without errors/crashes.

**Environment Information:**
N/A
**Configurations:**

`just validate "*"`

**Logs:**

topIssues.title: accept any op-program release in the fault proof game prestate checks
topIssues.author: tessr
topIssues.body:
Every new OP Chain needs a new op-program which includes their chain config. However, at the moment, we're checking for explicit governance approval of each op-program [see [here](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/blob/eeb0f8563c07430764ab0bb5f08eddf710813b0d/validation/fault_game_params_test.go#L97)]. In practice, this means that we're now requiring explicit governance approval for all new OP Chains... which is not what we want, nor what's specific in the standard rollup charter. 

Instead, we should check that the hash is present in this [list of op-program releases](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/develop/op-program/prestates/releases.json). This should be sufficient to ensure that a malicious chain operator cannot use their own modified/malicious op-program, a problem that @ajsutton highlighted [in Slack](https://oplabs-pbc.slack.com/archives/C05B4JVDGLV/p1732309708994439?thread_ts=1732309069.230899&cid=C05B4JVDGLV):

> We don't want to allow any absolute prestate - it's really important that it is something that faithfully implements the derivation process.
A malicious chain operator could theoretically deploy with a modified op-program that says they own all the money and could then post an invalid output root claiming they own all the money and the fault proof system would resolve in their favour and let them withdraw all the money.

Note that we should be fine to make these changes because we would not be modifying any of the "gov-approved" TOML files referenced in the charter. (Resolving https://github.com/orgs/ethereum-optimism/projects/58/views/4?pane=issue&itemId=86020829&issue=ethereum-optimism%7Cplatforms-team%7C438 would also make this clearer.)

topIssues.title: SuperchainRegistry: improve the diff tools
topIssues.author: geoknee
topIssues.body:
It should:
- [x] be extended to compute and print a diff for op-geth, too (see this function https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/blob/617815b4c1014fcf54cc482fd6ac54ba55237079/core/genesis.go#L259): https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/379
- [x] Let’s also improve it to post a comment on the PR like the k8s diff bot and not count as a CI failure. The comment can come with warnings: “did a hardfork timestamp change? triple check to avoid chain splits!”
- [ ] Let’s also improve it to print a diff when a *new* chain is added, not just a modification to an existing chain.
- [ ] Let's update the registry readme (adding a new chain section). It should explain that a diff should be expected and the PR author should check to see it makes sense. 
- [ ] It should handle changes in file name https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/actions/runs/9663016365/job/26654171032?pr=320 
---

topIssues.title: Consider storing all hardfork times explicitly in each chain's config file
topIssues.author: geoknee
topIssues.body:
I've been wondering if we can leverage/extend the existing codegen tooling to help keep this stuff tidy. It could:
1. throw an error if folks have set superchain_time in a way that doesn't make sense.
2. actually write all active hardforks into each chain's TOML file using the existing algorithm for resolving them from superchain-wide values + superchain_time + any overrides. We can then do the usual git diff --exit-code to ensure the modified TOMLs are checked in and reproducible.

Doing 2 has the advantage that hardfork times are no longer implicit / the result of an opaque resolution process, but there for all to see in the raw TOML files. We could also kill the diffbots (which are there to compute essentially the same thing) which are proving difficult to maintain in a secure way.
When we set e.g. the Isthmus time, we run codegen and it changes all existing chains' TOML files if appropriate. We see the diff in the actual Github diff, and don't need a bot to compute it and comment on the PR with the result.

topIssues.title: feature request: split `[addresses]` key into `[addresse.roles]` and `[addresses.protocol]`
topIssues.author: mds1
topIssues.body:
Right now I find the addresses section hard to read because it's a bit cluttered and there's nothing separating semantically different addresses: 

https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/blob/c92ef420eec2eaa83001f1fa13dd852bde3bbbf4/superchain/configs/mainnet/op.toml#L31-L53

I would suggest splitting this into `addresses.roles` and `addresses.contracts` keys, as shown below. This would then map nicely to the "roles" section of the [docs](https://docs.optimism.io/chain/security/privileged-roles). It also gives a similar structure to how inputs and outputs will be structured for the OP Stack Manager deployment scripts

I'm open to names other than "protocol" for the other section. I didn't want to use "contracts" as some roles are contracts, but protocol feels like it might be too broad of a term.

topPRs.title: ops: 'add chain' supports embedded contract artifacts
topPRs.author: bitwiseguy
topPRs.body:
# Problem

Previously we keyed off of `l1ContractsLocator` to determine which version of op-deployer to use when regenerating and comparing a standard genesis.json to one for a chain trying to enter the registry. Since contracts `tag://` locators were deprecated and replaced with the keyword `embedded`, we need to a new method to determine the appropriate version of op-contracts/op-deployer to use.

# Solution

This pr updates code for determining the appropriate op-deployer version to use when running genesis validations when a new chain enters the registry. It now does the following:

1. reads the opcm address from the state.json
2. scans through standard-versions.toml file to find an op-contracts entry with a matching opcm address
3. uses the op-contracts tag from [2] to map to the appropriate op-deployer version
